en: The Philippines is an archipelago composed of exactly 7,641 islands, with only about 2,000 of them inhabited.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering roughly 14,649 square kilometers.
The Sierra Madre is the longest mountain range in the Philippines, extending approximately 540 kilometers along Luzon's eastern coast.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an underground river that is navigable for about 8.2 kilometers.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of 223 meters.
Out of more than 200 volcanoes in the country, the Philippine Institute of Volcanology classifies exactly 24 as active.
The Philippines is administratively divided into 81 provinces, which are further grouped into 17 different regions.
The Philippines has a highly indented coastline that stretches for approximately 36,289 kilometers, making it the fifth longest globally.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a massive marine protected area covering exactly 97,030 hectares of pristine coral reefs.
